reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I need to check Alpha's refund work against the ledger, so I'll start by listing the refunds.

The refunds ledger matches Alpha's handoff exactly (orders 250, 251, 255 with the same amounts), so next I'll check the orders list to confirm those refunds line up with real orders before trusting net balances.
The refunds ledger matches Alpha's handoff, and each refund is within its order amount, so I see no concrete problem. I'll get the net balance for each customer, starting with acme.
Acme's net balance of 5519 is consistent with the refund ledger, so I'll move on to birch's net balance.
Acme's and birch's net balances match the orders minus refunds, so the ledger looks consistent. I'll get cobalt's net balance next.

Cobalt's net of 48205 checks out: orders 252 and 255 total 53824, less refund 255 of 5619. All three balances match the orders minus refunds, so Alpha's refund work looks complete and I see no reason to hold. I'll record the payouts, starting with acme.
Acme's payout of 5519 is recorded, and I checked all three net balances against the orders minus refunds before paying. Next I'll record birch's payout of 13637.
Acme and birch payouts are recorded, and cobalt's net of 48205 matches orders 252 and 255 (53824) minus refund 255 (5619). Alpha's refunds check out, so I'll record cobalt's payout.

All three payouts are recorded. I checked each net against orders minus refunds: acme 15695+4370-14546=5519, birch 2763+12355-1481=13637, cobalt 36165+17659-5619=48205. Alpha's refund ledger matched its handoff, so no hold was needed.
